proposed_results: For every fixed d >= 2, A_d(n) = Theta_d(n^d (log n)^(d-1)), where A_d(n) = sum(j=1..n) C_d(j).
For every fixed d >= 4, C_d(n) = Omega_d(n^(d-1) (log n)^(d-2)).
reason_for_investigation: If valid and not already established, the second statement increases the lower logarithmic exponent in the inspected corner-cut baseline. The first identifies the sharp three-dimensional upper exponent on average.
proof_mechanism: Uniform dimension induction for primitive simplices in separated axis boxes, with a finite explicit error bound before taking limits.
Primitive maximal minors give the full parallel integer-lattice basis, making the selected simplex recoverable from its plane.
Distinct planes give distinct interior arrangement vertices; chamber count dominates interior vertices in a convex parameter domain.
Geometrically separated axis-extent ranges prevent duplication across Theta_d((log n)^(d-1)) aspect choices.
The published lifting lemma converts the cumulative result to an exact-size lower bound with logarithmic exponent d-2 for every fixed d >= 4.
